extinctionDiscount.title: When extinction is the profitable choice
extinctionDiscount.subtitle: A profit-maximising owner picks the stock level that maximises present value. Slow growth and impatient capital move that level toward zero.

hint.impatient: With the discount rate above the growth rate, waiting for the population to breed earns less than cashing it out and reinvesting. The arithmetic recommends liquidation.
hint.patient: While the population grows faster than money does, leaving animals in the water is itself the better investment — the stock is an appreciating asset.

aria.conserve: Surplus production curve with the owner's optimal stock above the peak-yield point
aria.deplete: Surplus production curve with the owner's optimal stock below the peak-yield point
aria.liquidate: Surplus production curve with the owner's optimal stock at zero

extinctionDiscount.units: Stock in individuals; rates per year; price and cost in millions per unit.

reproductiveValue.title: Not every death costs the same
reproductiveValue.subtitle: Population growth is far more sensitive to breeding-female survival than to birth rate or calf survival. A hunt that targets mothers has found the most expensive class.

note.recover: to climb back from 30% to 80% of capacity
note.collapse: growth has been driven to zero or below

hint.female: This is the class the hunt actually targets. Removing breeding females strips the population of nearly all of its capacity to replace itself.
hint.other: Losses in this class hurt, but the population absorbs them. The growth rate lives almost entirely in adult female survival.

reproductiveValue.units: Sensitivities from cetacean matrix models; maximum productivity taken as 4% per year.

wildHarvestLadder.title: Tonnes for a teaspoon
wildHarvestLadder.subtitle: How much wild biomass each compound cost, and how industry eventually stopped paying it. Select a rung to compare.

axis.ratio: Kilograms of wild source per gram of product

note.course: destroyed to yield one 300 mg course

hint.escaped: Every terrestrial case on this ladder escaped wild harvest the same way: once the molecule was characterised, chemistry replaced collection. Wild harvest is the expensive route, not the cheap one.
hint.trapped: This is the one rung with no exit. Without a synthetic route the harvest never ends, and the ratio never improves — which is exactly why the population, not the chemistry, becomes the limiting resource.

aria.chart: Logarithmic comparison of wild biomass required per gram of product across five compounds

senescenceArrest.title: What "stops aging" would have to mean
senescenceArrest.subtitle: Mortality risk climbs exponentially with age. An intervention can postpone the climb, slow it, or — as claimed here — flatten it completely.

note.mrdt: years for mortality risk to double

hint.compress: Illness arrives later but the slope is unchanged: risk still doubles on the same clock, so the ceiling barely moves. This is what most successful medicine has achieved.
hint.decelerate: Bending the slope is the real target of geroscience. The best reproducible result on Earth — rapamycin in genetically diverse mice — moves median lifespan by roughly a tenth.
hint.arrest: Flatten the curve and death stops tracking age entirely; what remains is accident and injury. No compound has ever done this, in any organism, which is why the claim is a category apart rather than a bigger number.

aria.compress: Mortality curve shifted later but with an unchanged exponential slope
aria.decelerate: Mortality curve with a reduced exponential slope beside the untreated baseline
aria.arrest: Flat mortality curve with the exponential aging term removed entirely

senescenceArrest.units: Hazard on a logarithmic axis; baseline doubling time 8 years.

consentLadder.title: The ladder of consent
consentLadder.subtitle: Access law climbed one rung at a time, from open access to negotiated benefit-sharing. Select a rung to see what established it — and whether this trade clears it.

openAccess.label: Open access
openAccess.why: The trade operates exactly here: extraction without permission of any kind.

sovereignty.label: Sovereignty
sovereignty.why: No authority on Pandora is recognised as holding rights over its own biology.

consent.label: Prior informed consent
consent.why: No permission is sought, and no terms are negotiated with anyone.

benefit.label: Benefit-sharing
benefit.why: Every unit of value leaves the system; nothing returns to the world it came from.

personhood.label: Personhood
personhood.instrument: Legal standing of the being itself
personhood.why: This is the rung the case actually belongs on — and the one no access framework can reach.

hint.cleared: This is the only rung the trade satisfies, and it satisfies it by requiring nothing at all.
hint.failed: The trade fails this rung outright. Note that clearing every rung below the top would still leave the central problem untouched — those rungs govern property, and property is the wrong category here.
